definitions.gloss: chewy; firm; having a good bite; al dente
definitions.explanation: Describes noodles, mochi, or other starchy foods that have a pleasantly firm, springy texture — not soft or mushy. A desirable quality in Japanese noodle culture.

examples.japanese: このうどんは{腰|こし}がある。
examples.english: These udon noodles are nice and chewy.

examples.japanese: {腰|こし}のある{麺|めん}が{好|す}きです。
{讃岐|さぬき}うどんは{腰|こし}が{強|つよ}くて、{歯|は}ごたえがいい。
examples.english: Sanuki udon has a strong chewiness and great bite.

notes:
USAGE:
{腰|こし} here refers to the "body" or "backbone" of the noodle — its resilience and springiness. The opposite is {腰|こし}がない (soft, lacking firmness). Variations include {腰|こし}が{強|つよ}い (very firm) and {腰|こし}のある{麺|めん} (firm noodles, using the attributive form).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腰|こし}のある{麺|めん} (firm noodles)
- {腰|こし}が{強|つよ}い (very firm/chewy)
- {腰|こし}がない (soft, lacking firmness — negative)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Firmness ({腰|こし}) is considered a key quality indicator for udon and soba. {讃岐|さぬき}うどん from Kagawa Prefecture is famous for its strong {腰|こし}. The concept is similar to Italian "al dente" for pasta.
